title: Commitment Sundial — Fortnight Log
content:
Purpose:
A compact, two-week sprint notebook for tracking small bets on habits and output. The ‘sundial’ metaphor reminds me to map effort to time-of-day energy patterns (morning/afternoon/evening slots) rather than raw hours. Use this as a lightweight OKR sketch + rolling retro.

Window: 2026-02-20 -> 2026-03-05 (fortnight #4 of Q1)

Top-level intention (north star):
- Move one small user-facing feature from prototype -> shipped + gather first 50 qualitative feedback notes.
- Personal energy goal: sustain 4 high-focus slots per week (45-90m each).

Tripod metrics (quantitative anchors):
- Ship progress: milestone percentage for feature (current 40% -> target 100% by end of next fortnight)
- Feedback volume: 50 notes target (current 6)
- Focus slots: 4/week target (current avg 2.1)

Micro-OKRs (draft):
- Objective A: Prototype -> Beta deploy
  - KR1: Implement persistence + telemetry for the new routing knob (done: core schema)
  - KR2: Add telemetry events for 6 user journeys (in progress: 2)
  - KR3: Smoke-test integrations with Redwood Console routes (not started)

- Objective B: Personal throughput / rituals
  - KR1: Capture 8 post-session notes across fortnight (current 3)
  - KR2: Improve morning deep-work cadence to 4x/week (saw 2 last fortnight)

What I actually did (notes mid-cycle):
- Dev: Implemented schema changes and a quick local shim for telemetry. Broke into 3 small PRs to keep rollbacks easy.
- Product: Wrote a short 1-pager for internal stakeholders; Asha suggested adding a fallback story for legacy tenants.
- Habit: Hit two morning focus slots (both 75m), afternoon slots uneven because of meetings.

Evidence & metrics (quick table):
- Feature completion: 40% (schema + basic API + 2 telemetry events)
content_more:
- Feedback items captured: 6 (internal demos + hallway chats)
- Focus slots logged: 5 this fortnight (goal 8 over two weeks)
- Average slot length: 62 minutes

Notes to self / friction points:
- Context-switch tax is real on Tues/Thurs; move recurring meetings to Mon/Wed afternoon if possible.
- End-to-end telemetry still brittle; need small e2e test harness to validate events (low-effort, high-value).
- I tend to over-scope PRs; keep smallest-movable-piece principle and pair with SRE/infra when touching schema.

Hypotheses to test next window:
1) If I reserve 3 uninterrupted morning slots per week and put a single meeting-free buffer on Tuesdays, I’ll double morning throughput.
2) If I ship an early beta to 5 internal users and solicit structured feedback via a 3-question form, I’ll get 15 usable notes in a week.

Concrete experiments (next 2 weeks):
- Experiment 1: Calendar edit — block 10:00–11:30 M/W/Th as deep work. Status: planned.
- Experiment 2: Beta invite flow + 3-question feedback form (time to build: ~3h). Status: planned. Linked to JIRA-2142.
- Experiment 3: Lightweight e2e script that asserts telemetry events fire on the happy path. Status: backlog.

Quick todo list (ordered):
1. Create beta invite email template (30m) — assigned to me.
2. Add smoke tests for the telemetry shim (2h) — pair w/ Miguel.
3. Update internal 1-pager with fallback tenant story (15m) — ask Asha for gating criteria.
4. Reblock calendar and commit to morning slots for 2 weeks (5m).

Retro bullets (last fortnight):
- Wins: Broke work into smaller PRs which made reviews quicker; got clear product direction after the internal 1-pager.
- Misses: Didn’t prioritize e2e; meetings ate afternoons; feedback volume low because I postponed the invite.
- Surprises: Micro-commitments felt better than large uninterrupted days — helped reduce anxiety around scope.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Who within platform engineering is best to own the fallback tenant story for long-term? (Ping: @Miguel)
- Is there appetite to expose the routing knob in Redwood Console as an advanced toggle or keep it config-only? (Product decision)

Personal reflection (tone):
- I’m most productive when I have a short list of 2–3 explicit outcomes for the fortnight. This doc helps keep that list visible.
- Energy management beats arbitrary timeboxing; next cycle I want to be stricter about scheduling energy slots rather than ‘work hours’.

Next-cycle commitments (explicit):
- Ship to beta + collect 15 feedback notes.
- Run calendar experiment for two weeks (M/W/Th deep work).
- Add one small e2e test for telemetry.

Sprint sign-off (quick check):
- Confidence (0–10): 6
- Biggest risk: Meetings and unplanned infra incidents
- Backup plan: If infra takes priority, pivot to structured documentation + internal demo to keep momentum.
